newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom plans reorganisation, no break-up.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom plans reorganisation, no break-up.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom plans a wide-ranging reorganisation but will retain control of all units, Chairman Rem Vyakhirev said on Tuesday.
Gazprom, the world's biggest gas producer, plans to shed 100,000 jobs this year, saving three trillion roubles a year, he said.
"All of the internal blocs will remain within the Gazprom organisation," Vyakhirev told a news conference.
The government has targeted Gazprom, along with other monopolies such as national power company UES and the railways, for restructuring, but ministers have also said it will not be broken up.

Vyakhirev said he had agreed with First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov that he would retain control of a 35 percent state-owned stake in the company, which has been transferred to him under trust. He said some changes would be made to the trust agreement but gave no details.

Last week, following a row between Vyakhirev and senior ministers, privatisation minister Alfred Kokh said the government would review the arrangement under which Vyakhirev managed the 35 percent stake.
